meta.title: Tutorials · Aethyr docs
meta.description: Learn Aethyr by doing: short, story-driven tutorials covering reading Blueprints, editing, batches, data tables, materials and the live editor, plus the ones where something goes wrong and how to read it. Each has a video.

article.heading: Learn it by asking.
article.lead: Twenty-four short Rituals, each something you'd want to do: the exact sentence you'd say to your AI, and what Aethyr does under the hood. Every few Rituals, one shows something going wrong, because reading an error is a skill too. Each one has a short video. No tool memorization required, that's the whole point. Want one-line incantations instead? See the spellbook, or watch the Rituals.

note.html: Get the samples first. Most of these stories run on the Aethyr sample content. Ask your assistant: "Install the Aethyr samples." It builds them into a folder of their own and never overwrites your own assets. Run it again any time, because anything that already exists is skipped. A few stories (the project tour, the cleanup, the update check) use a small project of their own that the story builds first. Swap in your own assets there.

sections.heading: ① Read my Blueprint
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

You opened a project and there's a BP_Enemy nobody documented. Instead of clicking through every graph, ask.

youwhat does BP_Enemy do, event graph included?
Aethyr · your AI BP_Enemy is a Character with five variables and two functions. TakeDamage subtracts from Health and calls Die at zero, and BeginPlay just prints a greeting.
used summarize_blueprint → get_graph

Reads can't change anything, so this is the safest way to start. No need to enable writes. Great for code review and onboarding.

sections.heading: ② Onboard to a project you've never opened
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

You just cloned a UE project you have never seen, so map its shape without clicking through a hundred assets and without touching a single byte.

youi just pulled this repo and never opened it. what am i looking at?
Aethyr · your AI This is MyGame on engine 5.8, with 2 plugins enabled. Nothing here writes, because this is pure project metadata.
used get_project_metadata
youlist the blueprints in it, and explain the main one
Aethyr · your AI There are 6 Blueprints. I took BP_Enemy as the main one, the only Character, with 5 variables and 2 functions, and everything here was a read.
used list_blueprints → summarize_blueprint

Reads are free and fearless. Every call in this whole walkthrough is read-only, so you can map an unfamiliar project as aggressively as you like. Nothing here can dirty a package, trigger a save, or alter one node.

When you do start editing: the safety net is the same one the rest of the site shows. A ritual previews before it applies, every batch passes a compile gate, and the original .uasset is backed up before the first save, so a bad edit rolls back to exactly what you cloned.

sections.heading: ③ When the ritual fails
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

Errors happen. With the aethyr-triage skill, they're legible instead of cryptic.

youi asked for BP_Enemyy and got BlueprintNotFound for /Game/AethyrSamples/AI/BP_Enemyy. what went wrong?
Aethyr · your AI There is no Blueprint called BP_Enemyy at that path, because of the extra y. The folder has BP_Enemy, so I read that instead, and neither call changed any asset.
used read_blueprint ×2

A failed call changes nothing. The error names the tool and the path it could not find, so you can fix the input and ask again. Both calls here were reads, and the first one never touched an asset.

sections.heading: ④ Say it, don't wire it
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

You want a dash. You could place the nodes by hand, or you could describe it. The sample project has no player Blueprint, so the dash goes on BP_Enemy.

yougive BP_Enemy a dash, with a 2 second cooldown so it can't be spammed
Aethyr · your AI I added bCanDash and DashCooldown, then a Dash function that launches the character forward and resets the flag after the cooldown. It compiled with no errors.
used apply_ops → compile_function ×2

Under the hood: with the aethyr-edit skill installed, your AI assembles the whole function as one unit and runs compile_function to confirm it builds, so you get a working node graph, not a pile of disconnected nodes.

sections.heading: ⑤ All or nothing
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

Renames and restructures are where things break. Make the AI do it as a single transaction that either fully lands or fully reverts.

yourename Health to CurrentHealth and clamp it to MaxHealth. all in one go, and show me a preview first
Aethyr · your AI The dry run has one rename and a new ClampHealth event that clamps CurrentHealth to MaxHealth, with no conflicts. Apply it?
used preview_ops
yougo ahead and apply it
Aethyr · your AI Applied as one batch and compiled. If the clamp had failed to compile, the rename would have rolled back with it.
used apply_ops

Why preview? preview_ops is a read-only dry run: it tells you exactly what a batch will touch before a single byte is written. The aethyr-edit skill teaches the AI to always offer it for multi-step edits.

sections.heading: ⑥ When it won't compile
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

You tidy up a Blueprint by deleting a function nothing seems to use, and now it will not compile. Aethyr compiles on request, reads the error back to you in plain words, and the fix is one call. This picks up where ① and ④ left BP_Enemy.

youdelete the Die function from BP_Enemy, i don't think anything calls it
Aethyr · your AI I deleted Die and compiled, and BP_Enemy fails because it could not find a function named Die. TakeDamage still calls it when Health reaches zero.
used delete_function → compile_blueprint
youput it back so it compiles
Aethyr · your AI I added an empty Die function, so TakeDamage binds to it again and BP_Enemy compiles with no errors. Give it a body, or move the call.
used add_function → compile_blueprint

The error names what is missing. A compile reads the Blueprint and reports, it does not rewrite your graph, so you can fix the cause and compile again as often as you like. The compile is also your check after any delete: it lists every call that lost its target.

sections.heading: ⑦ Summon a working pickup
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

The sample pickup has a body and no behavior: a mesh, a trigger sphere and a heal amount. By the end of this exchange it heals on touch, compiled clean, just from describing it.

youlook at BP_HealthPickup. what's in it so far?
Aethyr · your AI BP_HealthPickup is an Actor with a Mesh and a Trigger sphere, and one variable, HealAmount, which defaults to 25. There is no overlap handler yet, so touching it does nothing.
used summarize_blueprint → get_components
younow when something overlaps the trigger, heal it by HealAmount. preview first
Aethyr · your AI The handler binds the Trigger's begin-overlap event, reads HealAmount, and applies it as negative damage. The preview says all 10 operations are valid.
used preview_ops
youlooks right. apply it
Aethyr · your AI It is applied as one unit and BP_HealthPickup compiles with no errors and no warnings.
used apply_ops

Under the hood: the whole handler went in as one apply_ops batch wrapped in a single undo transaction. Either every node and wire lands together or none does, so the graph never sits half-built between calls.

Look before you leap: preview_ops renders the exact changes without writing a byte, so you see the shape of the handler before it reaches the asset. The compile result comes back in the apply_ops reply, so there is nothing more to run.

Safety net: batches pass a compile gate before they save, and single writes save as they go. Either way the existing .uasset is copied to a timestamped backup before the first save of the session. If a change goes wrong, restore the backup over the file while no editor holds it. Reads never mutate anything.

sections.heading: ⑧ Grow a bare stat into a system
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

BP_Enemy keeps its health in a lone Health float. You want a tidier system around it, without ever leaving the asset half-rewritten.

youwhat variables does BP_Enemy have right now?
Aethyr · your AI BP_Enemy has five variables, and none of them is in a category. TakeDamage subtracts from Health, but nothing keeps it under MaxHealth.
used list_variables
yourename Health to CurrentHealth, put it and MaxHealth under a Vitals category, and add a Heal function
Aethyr · your AI The rename and both category moves landed together, and Heal compiled cleanly after them. BP_Enemy has no errors and no warnings.
used apply_ops → compile_function

All or nothing: the rename and both category moves went in as one apply_ops batch behind the compile gate. If that batch had failed to compile, none of it would have landed. Heal followed as its own compile_function call, because a preview can't bind a new function's entry node. A backup is written before the first save, either way.

Reads are free, so look first: list_variables never mutates and costs you nothing within a turn. Confirming the starting shape before you plan a change is the cheap habit that makes the expensive step safe.

sections.heading: ⑨ Fork a proven Blueprint into a variant
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

You have a working BP_Enemy and you want a meaner sibling, BP_EliteEnemy, that shares every line of logic but hits harder.

youmake a copy of BP_Enemy called BP_EliteEnemy, same parent and setup
Aethyr · your AI BP_Enemy's parent is Character, so I duplicated it as BP_EliteEnemy. It has the same variables, functions and graphs, wired exactly the same.
used read_blueprint → duplicate_blueprint
youmake it elite: 250 health and speed 450
Aethyr · your AI I changed only three defaults on BP_EliteEnemy. Health and MaxHealth went from 100 to 250, and Speed from 300 to 450, with no graph edits.
used set_variable_default ×3

Why duplicate, not rebuild: duplicate_blueprint copies the whole asset in one call, so the elite's logic is the proven logic, not a re-drawing you have to re-verify. Hand copy-paste is where a missed connection hides.

Safety net: single writes like these defaults save as they go, so the backup written before the first save is your way back. Nothing in this story touches your working BP_Enemy, which stays exactly as it was.

sections.heading: ⑩ When a batch goes sideways
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

A batch trips on one operation, and the whole thing rolls back untouched, exactly the safety net you want.

yougive BP_Turret a TargetActor variable and make Fire apply damage to it. do it all in one batch
Aethyr · your AI The batch failed at step 7: a TargetActor reference can't wire into ApplyDamage's Controller pin. Nothing was written, so BP_Turret is untouched.
used apply_ops
youfix that step and show me a preview before you apply it
Aethyr · your AI The fix is a Cast To Controller node feeding that pin. The dry run says all 12 operations are valid, and nothing has been written.
used preview_ops
yougood, apply it
Aethyr · your AI Applied as one batch, and BP_Turret compiles with no errors.
used apply_ops

Why this is safe: a batch apply_ops is atomic. Every op runs against an in-memory copy and the result must pass the compile gate before a single byte hits disk. One bad op fails the whole batch, and the on-disk asset stays exactly as it was, no half-written graph to clean up.

The loop that pays off: when a step fails, the error names the offending op and the pin, so you fix one thing, not the batch. Re-run preview_ops to validate with zero writes, then apply_ops once it's green. The aethyr-triage skill walks this read, fix, re-preview loop.

sections.heading: ⑪ A designer's balance pass, no editor needed
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

You suspect a loot drop is overtuned, and you want to reason about it without opening the editor or touching a single asset.

youpull up DT_Loot. does anything look off?
Aethyr · your AI Legendary_Sword sits at weight 90, more than double the next row. A Legendary item with the highest drop weight in the table looks like a mistake.
used read_data_table
youif i nerf it, who else is affected?
Aethyr · your AI BP_Enemy's LootTable variable defaults to DT_Loot, so a weight change shifts every drop it rolls. That came from reading variables, not the reference graph, because a plain name is not a hard reference.
used list_variables

Reads are cheap and safe. Every step here was a read: the table and the Blueprint variables. Nothing was loaded for write, and no .uasset changed on disk. You can trace a balance question end to end and walk away with the editor still untouched.

When you do decide to act, the edit is a separate, deliberate step. The change lands with an automatic backup written before the first save. Story ⑫ makes that edit on this table.

sections.heading: ⑫ A loot table that needs rebalancing
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

Players are drowning in legendary swords. Somebody typed a drop weight wrong, or somebody lied about it. Either way, DT_Loot needs a look.

youfind the loot table and show me what's in it
Aethyr · your AI DT_Loot has 5 rows. The everyday items sit at weights between 8 and 40, but Legendary_Sword sits at 90, which is generous.
used list_data_tables → read_data_table
youdrop the sword to 2, and add a Legendary_Goblet at weight 1
Aethyr · your AI Legendary_Sword went from 90 to 2, and the tool echoed both values. Legendary_Goblet is a new row at weight 1, and the row name was free, so nothing was overwritten.
used set_data_row_value → add_data_row

Read before you write: read_data_table is the cheap way to orient before you change a row. set_data_row_value takes the new value in its string form and hands back what it replaced. add_data_row refuses to clobber an existing row name unless you pass overwrite:true.

sections.heading: ⑬ A row that won't take
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

A DataTable edit is the easiest thing in the world until a row name has a typo in it. Aethyr names the row it could not find, writes nothing, and the retry is one call. This builds on ⑪ and ⑫, and the same DT_Loot.

youset the weight on Legendary_Sord to 2
Aethyr · your AI That failed: there is no row called Legendary_Sord in DT_Loot, and nothing was changed. I read the table, and the closest row is Legendary_Sword.
used set_data_row_value → read_data_table
youtypo, sorry. use Legendary_Sword
Aethyr · your AI Done. The Weight on Legendary_Sword went from 90 to 2, and the tool echoed both values so you can see it landed.
used set_data_row_value

A failed write changes nothing. The error carries the tool, the row and the table, so you know exactly what to fix. Reading the table first is the cheap way to find the real row name.

sections.heading: ⑭ The boss fight that is too easy
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

Playtesters beat your final boss in forty seconds. One of them used a pool noodle. Time to find out why BP_Boss is a pushover.

youhow does the boss take damage? playtesters are bored
Aethyr · your AI BossTakeDamage subtracts the damage from BossHealth and stops there, with no zero check and no phases. BossHealth and BossMaxHealth both default to 50.
used summarize_blueprint → get_function
youraise its health to 1500 and add an enrage below 30 percent health. preview before you apply
Aethyr · your AI I set both defaults to 1500, then dry-ran the enrage branch as a batch. Every operation is valid and it touches one asset. Apply it?
used set_variable_default ×2 → preview_ops
yougo ahead and apply it
Aethyr · your AI Applied as one batch and BP_Boss compiles. The boss has 1500 health and sets bEnraged once it drops to 30 percent. The pool noodle still does 1 damage.
used apply_ops

Read small, then bigger: summarize_blueprint tells you how big a thing is for almost nothing, and get_function pulls one function body. Open the big payloads only when you know they are worth it.

One write, then a batch: set_variable_default is a single write, so each call saves as it goes (with a backup before the asset's first save). The multi-step part went through apply_ops, which only saves if the whole batch compiles.

sections.heading: ⑮ The menu typo, the night before the demo
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

It is 11 pm. The demo is at 9 am. The main menu says "Strat Game". You could fix this in the UMG designer, or you could ask.

youWBP_MainMenu has a typo on the start button. show me the widget tree
Aethyr · your AI WBP_MainMenu has a VerticalBox of three buttons, and each has a TextBlock. The one under PlayButton is PlayLabel, and it reads "Strat Game".
used read_widget_blueprint
youfix it to "Start Game", and add a "DEMO BUILD" label
Aethyr · your AI PlayLabel now reads "Start Game", and a new TextBlock named DemoBadge under the buttons says "DEMO BUILD".
used set_widget_property → add_widget → set_widget_property
youcompile it
Aethyr · your AI It compiled with no errors. The typo is gone and the badge is in, so go to bed.
used compile_widget_blueprint

Under the hood: add_widget and set_widget_property are for UMG trees. Blueprint graph nodes still go through add_node. Each of these is a single write, so it saves as it goes, with a backup before the asset's first save.

sections.heading: ⑯ The turret that will not fire
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

The turret is in the level. It compiles, it is alive, and it does absolutely nothing, with great confidence. Read the turret first. Then take a look at the empty behavior tree next door.

youwhy does BP_Turret never shoot?
Aethyr · your AI Fire only prints its line when FireRate is above zero, and FireRate defaults to 0.0. It is one very patient turret.
used get_function → list_variables
youset it to 2. also the enemy just stands around, show me its behavior tree
Aethyr · your AI FireRate is now 2.0. BT_Enemy has no nodes yet, and its blackboard BB_Enemy has 4 keys.
used set_variable_default → read_behavior_tree

Read before you guess: read_behavior_tree lists every node with its class, kind and parent, plus the linked blackboard and its keys. A zero in a variable and an empty tree both show up in one read. Want to see the turret fire for real? Story ⑱ drives the running editor.

sections.heading: ⑰ A value the editor won't parse
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

Some values are not plain numbers. A behavior tree's Wait node keeps its time in a small struct, so a bare 0.6 is not something it can parse. The error says what failed, and the struct form works first time. This picks up the empty tree from ⑯.

youput a Sequence at the root of BT_Enemy with a Wait of 0.6 seconds under it
Aethyr · your AI The Sequence and the Wait went in, but a bare 0.6 for WaitTime failed to parse. The time is a struct with a DefaultValue and a Key, so it has to be written that way.
used add_bt_node ×2 → set_bt_node_property
youok, set it that way then
Aethyr · your AI WaitTime is set to (DefaultValue=0.6,Key=""), so the Wait node now waits 0.6 seconds instead of the default 5.
used set_bt_node_property

Struct values go in as text. When a property is a struct, give it in the same form the editor shows it, with every member named. The old value comes back in the reply, so you can check the change.

sections.heading: ⑱ Prove it in the running editor
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

The turret is fixed on paper. Now watch it work. This one needs an editor open on your project, and the Epic bridge also needs Epic's own MCP running inside that editor.

youis my editor responding? if it is, drop a BP_Turret into the level
Aethyr · your AI The editor is healthy and its game thread is responsive, so it is not stalled on a breakpoint. I spawned a BP_Turret in the level.
used health_check → spawn_actor
younow press play and tell me whether it actually runs
Aethyr · your AI A play session started through Epic's bridge, and the state said is_playing is true. I stopped it again, so the editor is back as you left it.
used epic_call_tool → get_pie_state → epic_call_tool

Native tool or bridge? Aethyr's own tools handle Blueprint graphs, assets and the common editor actions. Things like Play In Editor, the viewport and selection go through epic_call_tool. You pick a toolset with epic_list_toolsets, learn its functions with epic_describe_toolset, and then call one by its wire name.

Bridged writes follow the same rules: a session started read-only refuses write-shaped bridge calls, just like any other Aethyr write. If the bridge says it is not reachable, its discovery tools tell you what is missing.

sections.heading: ⑲ Who broke the turret?
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

Yesterday the turret fired twice a second. Today it fires never. Somebody checked something in. Look at the evidence without blaming anyone out loud. On a project with source control, get_asset_history lists the revisions. The sample project has none, so this story shows the answer you get without it and reads the value directly.

youthe turret stopped firing. show me the last few changes to BP_Turret
Aethyr · your AI Source control answered with a plain reason instead of a list: source control is not enabled. So there is no history to read, and I have not touched the asset.
used get_asset_history
youok, no history. what's FireRate on it right now? it used to be 2
Aethyr · your AI FireRate is 0.0, which is why the turret never fires. You said it used to be 2.0, so that is the likely change.
used list_variables
youput it back to 2
Aethyr · your AI FireRate is back to 2.0, so the turret fires again.
used set_variable_default

Old revisions use the normal read tools: load_asset_revision returns a temp asset path that read_blueprint, summarize_blueprint, get_graph and read_data_table accept as is. When you are done, unload_packages with temp_revisions:true frees it.

Try it on a project with source control: set FireRate to 2.0 on the turret, submit it, set it back to 0.0, submit again, and you have the full version of this story.

sections.heading: ⑳ Lava that glows like a lighthouse
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

The art director says the lava is "a bit much". Players can see it from orbit. Good news, you do not need to open the material editor.

youwhich knobs does the lava material expose, and what is MI_Lava_Hot set to?
Aethyr · your AI M_Lava exposes EmissiveStrength, FlowSpeed and GlowColor. MI_Lava_Hot has EmissiveStrength at 12.0, and twelve is the problem.
used read_material → get_material_instance_params
youdrop the glow to 3, and make a cooler instance called MI_Lava_Cool
Aethyr · your AI EmissiveStrength on MI_Lava_Hot is now 3.0, and MI_Lava_Cool exists as a new instance of M_Lava, ready for its own overrides.
used set_material_instance_parameter → create_material_instance

Instance versus base: set_material_instance_parameter overrides one parameter on an instance and leaves the parent alone. To change the base material's own default, the tool for that is set_material_parameter.

sections.heading: ㉑ Spring cleaning the Content folder
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

Your Props folder has duplicate names and a BP_OldDoor that everyone is afraid of. Tidy it, with a net under you.

yougive me an inventory of Props by folder, and flag anything off
Aethyr · your AI There are 4 assets in 3 folders under Props, all read from the asset registry. The flag is duplicate_name on BP_Barrel, which lives in two folders.
used list_assets
youthere is an old door in Doors, BP_OldDoor. rename it to BP_WoodenDoor, same folder
Aethyr · your AI Nothing points at BP_OldDoor, so the rename is safe, and it is now BP_WoodenDoor. If anything had referenced it, those references would have been fixed up.
used get_referencers → move_asset

Impact first: get_referencers is a fast registry read, so check what depends on an asset before you move or delete it.

sections.heading: ㉒ The delete that said no
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

Deleting an asset something else still uses is how levels fill up with invisible barrels. Aethyr's delete asks the reference graph first and refuses, handing back who is still using the asset. This continues the cleanup from ㉑.

youdelete the old BP_Barrel in the Misc folder
Aethyr · your AI Not deleted. BP_BarrelChild still references it, and the refusal named it. A forced delete would leave that reference empty, so I did not force it.
used delete_asset
youfine, delete the child first
Aethyr · your AI I deleted BP_BarrelChild, then BP_Barrel. Nothing pointed at the barrel any more, so the second delete went through.
used delete_asset ×2

IMPORTANT: delete_asset with force=true deletes anyway and leaves dangling references as nulls. Ask for a force only when you have seen the referencer list and you are sure. It only works on /Game and project-plugin content.

sections.heading: ㉓ Is the wizard awake? And is the spellbook current?
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

Tools hang, or answers look stale, or you just want to know if Aethyr is up to date. Two tools cover that.

youaethyr feels slow. is it me or is it the editor?
Aethyr · your AI The editor is healthy and its game thread is answering, so it is not stalled on a dialog or a breakpoint. The report shows update_available as false, with the current version at 0.7.0-1435.
used health_check
youis there a newer version? show me what updating would do, but don't install anything
Aethyr · your AI In preview mode it only reports, and it says up_to_date: the current version is 0.7.0-1435 and the latest is v0.7.0-1435, so there is nothing to download.
used apply_update

Ask first: your AI should only call apply_update with confirm:true after you say yes. It previews by default. On the Fab build, apply_update is not registered at all because Fab updates the plugin itself. Update through Fab there.

sections.heading: ㉔ When nothing is playing
sections.html:
▶ Watch this ritual

Some commands only make sense while the game is running. Ask for one with no play session and Aethyr passes Epic's answer straight back. It points back to ⑱, where a session was started on purpose.

youstop the play session
Aethyr · your AI There is no play session to stop. Epic's bridge answered that a play session is not currently running, and nothing was changed.
used epic_call_tool
youok, start one so i can see it runs, then stop it
Aethyr · your AI I started a play session and stopped it again, so the editor is back as you left it.
used epic_call_tool ×2

Check first when you are not sure. get_pie_state says whether a session is running, and it never changes anything. The play commands themselves go through epic_call_tool.
